govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FlyingEagleMoti: This letter from Sean Mansfield of Flying Eagle Motion Pictures is a filmmaker’s note. Filmmakers chased the JFK story. Hollywood loved the case. The project was ambitious. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PicturesTomAlye: This postal return receipt fragment — creator unknown — is a mail record. Return receipts proved delivery. The fragment is a curiosity. Mail was the lifeline. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of office history.
legends-that-every-child-should-know-a-s: Editor Hamilton Wright Mabie selects the great legends of the world — King Arthur, Roland, Siegfried, and more — retold for young readers. Each tale carries the heroism and wonder that have thrilled children for centuries. A splendid introduction to the story-treasures every child deserves to know.
cytherea: Joseph Hergesheimer's novel follows a respectable middle-aged man who abandons his orderly life in pursuit of an idealized love. His quest for Cytherea — the goddess of beauty — leads him through disillusion and self-discovery. A searching, beautifully written study of desire in Jazz Age America.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acacius-bisho: This 1913 reference article on Acacius of Beroea — the aged bishop, friend of Chrysostom. Cornelius Clifford recounts his long life. He bridged the Antiochene quarrels. A peacemaker of the early Church. He lived past a hundred, honored by all. His letters survive as models of charity.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrew-of-cae: A 1913 entry on Andrew of Caesarea — the commentator on Revelation. Anthony Maas honors his ancient work. His notes guided the Greek Church. The Apocalypse found its first guide. A bishop among the exegetes. His text is the oldest on Revelation.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arethas-of-ca: A 1913 entry on Arethas of Caesarea — the Byzantine bishop and scholar. Thomas Shahan honors his learned notes. His scholia lit the Apocalypse. The manuscripts preserve his hand. A prelate among the bookmen. His library held the ancient manuscripts. His see guarded the Cappadocian plain.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aurea: This 1913 reference piece on Aurea — a name in the martyrs' story. The entry preserves her modest fame. The old calendars keep her name. The Church honors its ancient witnesses. A virgin of the early Church. Her feast graces the August calendar.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bagnorea: A 1913 entry on Bagnorea — Bagnoregio, St. Bonaventure's birthplace. Umberto Benigni honors its seraphic son. The dying town crowns its cliff. The Franciscan doctor was born here. The cradle of the Seraphic Doctor. Its Civita crumbles on its pinnacle. Its bishop's palace crowns the rock.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-balanaea: A 1913 entry on Balanaea — the Syrian coastal city, now a titular see. Siméon Vailhé notes its Christian past. Its bishops graced the old councils. The sea guards its ruined site. A see of the Levantine shore. Its bishops signed the ancient creeds.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-basil-of-amas: A 1913 entry on Basil of Amasea — the martyr bishop. Johann Peter Kirsch honors his death. He died for the faith's sake. The entry preserves his modest fame. A bishop of the persecution age. His feast graces the April calendar. His see guarded the Pontic coast.
